newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 1.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- Five men were still being questioned by Irish police in County Donegal on Thursday after being arrested in suspicious circumstances near Malin Head.
- The largest number of bonfires in Dublin for a number of years could be seen burning throughout the city on Halloween Night on Thursday.
- Irish consumers face significant price increases in a wide range of goods including food, magazines and clothing, if the punt remains at its current low level of just above parity against sterling.

- The 51 million pound acquisition of The Mortgage Corporation in Britain by First National Building society has led to a downgrading of the Irish society's financial strength by international rating agency Moody's.
- Scottish Radio Holdings has confirmed it is paying 500,000 Irish pounds for its 15 per cent stake in Radio Ireland, a move that values the second national radio operator at 3.3 million punts.
- The Norwegian oil company Statoil will begin testing the Connemara oilfield in March next year in the first of 11 wells that will be drilled on the oilfield off the coast of Galway.
- A senior executive at RTE, Ireland's national broadcasting company, has resigned in a scandal over "financial irregularities" which may involve up to 100,000 Irish pounds.

- Irish police were on Thursday trying to solve the mystery of what five men were doing on the Donegal coastline when they were arrested with an inflatable boat, camouflage netting and radio equipment.
-Tutsi rebels appeared to have taken control of Bukavu, Zaire's fourth largest city, and were poised to capture another provincial capital as the war along the Zaire-Rwanda border intensified.

- Ireland's state industrial development authority, IDA Ireland, confirmed that there was a shortage of highly qualified personnel to work in the upper echelons of new companies which had opened in the International Financial Services Centre.
- A new statutory body to ensure that all takeovers are operated in a "fair and reasonable manner" is to be set up under a bill tabled by junior Minister Pat Rabbitte in parliament.
